extracted.intended_audience: students and mercantile practitioners learning manual arithmetic (historical Italian abacus/arithmetic methods)
extracted.subtask_description: A historical instructional excerpt describing practical rules and procedures for performing addition, subtraction, grouping, carrying/borrowing, and checking results in various bases/denominations for use in commerce and calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align numbers by place (ones, tens, hundreds, ...)
rubrics_metrics.description: When adding or subtracting, place figures in columns according to their denomination (ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, etc.) so that corresponding places line up (la riga corno vedi qui, metti fotto la riga fotto il filo dei numeri).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text repeatedly instructs to write numbers one under another by place (fila, filo, riga) — e.g., put units under units, tens under tens, hundreds under hundreds — before performing column-wise operations. Examples show writing ones, tens, hundreds, thousands in separate rows/columns and then summing or subtracting column by column.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add columnwise and carry when a column reaches the base
rubrics_metrics.description: Add figures in each column (frequenti / giogniali) and when the sum in a column equals or exceeds the base (e.g., 10 in decimal or other base), reduce that column and carry (congiunto / la pua) the excess to the next higher place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The procedure: add all digits in a column, write down the remainder for that place and carry the integral part to the next place. The text gives many worked examples (e.g., forming filas of ones, tens, hundreds) and notes forming carries repeatedly until all higher places are adjusted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group digits into denominations for convenient summing
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect and group figures into denomination-rows (ones, tens, dozens, hundreds, thousands, etc.) before summing to simplify the addition (recoglier le figure, fare la pua de la summa).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author recommends collecting numbers of the same 'nature' and summing them group-by-group, then combining the group-sums using the place-value carries; several patterns and tables are shown for doing this efficiently for large lists of quantities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce full groups (discard complete base-units) and keep remainders
rubrics_metrics.description: When summing, discard complete groups equal to the base (e.g., groups of 9, 7, 12 depending on system) by 'getting rid' of such full groups and only keeping the remainder for the current place (gettare via tutti li novenarij / togliere le fette che fanno il tale numero).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text explains procedures where one repeatedly removes full groups (novenarij, septenarii, etc.) and retains the leftover units; this is used both for base-reduction and checking consistency. Examples illustrate removing sets and collecting remainders for further operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use auxiliary lines/filo (help rows) to facilitate carries and remainders
rubrics_metrics.description: Set down auxiliary rows or 'filo' to store intermediate groupings and to manage carries and subtractions when direct operations are awkward (metti fotto la riga fotto il filo dei numeri; usare 'aiuto').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual shows using extra written rows (filo, fila) for ones/tens/hundreds to move figures between places, to collect those to be carried, and to compute subtractions by creating helper quantities. This is recommended when numbers are large or operations must be split.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subtraction: subtract smaller from the larger and borrow when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: In subtraction (sustraçione), always subtract the smaller number from the larger; if a digit in a place cannot be subtracted because it is smaller, borrow (abattere / farce aiuto) from the next higher place following usual borrowing rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text emphasizes that one must not try to subtract a greater from a smaller in the same place without borrowing. It describes borrowing (abattere) and auxiliary procedures (fare aiuto) to perform the subtraction by moving units from higher places, and gives examples showing the borrowing steps and how to restore results to memory.

rubrics_metrics.name: When direct subtraction is impossible, create an 'aid' by removing/adding appropriate units
rubrics_metrics.description: If a direct subtraction cannot be performed (lack of sufficient units in a place), construct an auxiliary subtraction by taking units from higher places and adjusting (fare aiuto / fen^a aiuto) so the operation becomes feasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several methods are shown: reorganize figures (metti l'uno sopra l'altro), use the fila/filo arrangement to make a new row that supplies needed units, and then perform the subtraction; the manual gives concrete worked examples (e.g., combining specific place values to form the needed borrow).

rubrics_metrics.name: Work in the correct base/denomination and adapt carry/borrow rules accordingly
rubrics_metrics.description: Operations must respect the numeral system or unit denominations in use (e.g., base 10 or other bases like 7, 9, 12; or compound units like soldi/libre) — carries and discards occur at the system's unit size (quando la pua raggiunge la base, ridurre).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text repeatedly shows examples in various moduli (novenary, septenary, duodecimal, and commercial money/measure denominations). It instructs adjusting how many units are carried/removed according to that system (e.g., when groups reach 12, carry to the next column).

rubrics_metrics.name: Check sums by casting out base-groups (casting-out-nines style checks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the removal of full base-groups (e.g., novenarii) as a means of checking computations: if after removing such groups the expected remainders align, the sum is likely correct (tetuvoi sapere code quello acada: cioe ebe raro riga ... toglia i novenarii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author suggests removing full groups repeatedly and comparing the remaining remainders with those expected; examples illustrate that if the same remainder appears when recomputing in different ways, this supports correctness. This behaves like a historical analogue of casting-out-nines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convert compound units (money, measures) to common smallest denomination before summing
rubrics_metrics.description: When summing different denominations (weights, currencies, measures), convert each quantity into the common smallest unit (per la tavola / secondo le valute e misure) and then perform placewise addition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual refers to mercantile practice: put quantities into a table according to local currencies/measures, convert using the local rates, and then sum the converted quantities; afterwards reconvert grouped sums into higher denominations (soldo, denari, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect repeated contributions iteratively to build totals (successive addition)
rubrics_metrics.description: When many quantities must be summed, add them iteratively in manageable blocks (collect a number of rows, sum them, then add the block-sums), reducing and carrying between steps until the total is obtained (aggiungere a uno a uno, poi sommare le somme).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text advises adding numbers one by one into a running total, or forming sub-tables of group sums, then combining those sub-sums; this prevents loss and simplifies carry management for very many addends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Represent numbers of the same 'nature' together to reveal patterns and ease reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Place numbers of the same type or periodicity adjacent in the layout so that their mutual relationships (varieties, frequenze) become visible and reduction/cancellation is easier (mettere le quantità pari, le medesime parti insieme).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several passages recommend arranging similar numbers together (e.g., same residual patterns, same remainders when divided by the base) to exploit cancellations and simplify both addition and checking. Examples show grouping by residues and using those patterns to accelerate computation.

rubrics_metrics.name: When summing in multiple different modes, prefer simpler/more practiced rules for reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Although there are many possible algorithms ('piu modi'), the manual recommends learning a few good, reliable methods thoroughly rather than many awkward ones; practice the chosen rules to gain speed and reduce mistakes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text warns that many strange or ad-hoc methods exist and that habitual practice of the standard rules (alignment, column addition, carrying, borrowing, use of helper rows) yields the best results — i.e., pedagogy/advice about method selection and instruction.
